newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares closed lower on Monday, but the drop was less than expected as the market recovered slightly from a 1.5 percent lower opening.
The AEX share index closed just over 1.1 percent, or 8.17 points, lower at 716.21. The index hit a day's low at 712.21.
Dealers said that investors were closely watching Wall Street, since another fall could pull the Dutch index as low as 680 points.
"If the AEX index falls close to the level of 680 points it would be the time to buy again," said one dealer.
Dutch chartists said the index would remain volatile.

"We expect the market to remain volatile over the next few weeks and only a break out of the 700-745 trading range will signal a clear technical picture," said one Dutch chartist, another said the clue might come from Wall Street this week.
Another factor that could disturb the market is Friday's option expiry. "The expiry could also put pressure on prices," said one dealer.
Financials were among the shares hit hardest.
Bank-insurer ING fell more than its sector rivals, declining 2.20 guilders to 71.00.
Dealers said there was a fair amount of selling of ING call options at the moment.
"If the index falls further as result of interest rate worries, this is likely to put extra pressure on financial stocks," one said.
Some feel that Tuesday's U.S. CPI data could be another spur to the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates again, if the March figure is strong.
Music and movies group Polygram was an exception in an overall depressed market, since the stock rose 0.70 guilders to 93.00 guilders.
Copier maker Oce van der Grinten fell 4.00 guilders to 233.00 ahead of Tuesday's first quarter results.
Dealers expect Oce to recover tomorrow as expectations for first quarter results, to be announced after the bourse closes, are good.
Electronics firm Philips slipped only 0.10 guilders to 86.20. "Volumes in Philips were low, but at least it managed to fall much less than the overall market," said one dealer.
Builder BAM Group was down one guilder at 127.90, despite merger news. BAM said earlier it was in merger talks with sector rival Wilma.
